messages:
alex: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel_selector change i'm seeing a ~12-18% p95 latency regression on llama3-13b (seq=1024, bs=4). KV cache hit rate looks the same. @mira @sam any ideas?

mira: i noticed a blip in CI too. early signs point to the head-dim specific matmul path we enabled (frac-head optimized GEMM). can you paste repro?

alex: repro steps: `./perf/run_infer.sh --model llama3-13b --seq 1024 --bs 4 --template chat_slim --rope_theta=100.0` on A100-80GB. p95 moved from 98ms -> 113ms after the selector change. kv hits ~99.6%. cpu pinned.

sam: try forcing the legacy kernel selector to confirm. i suspect the new selector is choosing the quant-friendly kernel for head_dim=128 that has worse perf for long sequences.

alex: ran with legacy: `KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy ./perf/run_infer.sh --model llama3-13b --seq 1024 --bs 4 --template chat_slim --rope_theta=100.0`. p95 = 99ms. so it's definitely selector-related.

perf-bot: profile upload: https://perf.internal/reports/1789912345 — aggregate flame shows hotspot in `matmul_head_frac` and `kv_read_dispatch`.

mira: posting quick profile snippet:
```
# top hotspots (self):
0. matmul_head_frac : 34.2%
1. kv_read_dispatch  : 12.1%
2. rmsnorm_fwd      : 8.7%
3. attention_gemm   : 7.9%
# kernel selected: gemm_frac_v2 for head_dim=128, rope_theta=100.0
```

kai: two quick notes: (1) the selector change added rope_theta heuristics (it now biases kernels when rope_theta > 90), (2) batching heuristics also changed microbatch split thresholds — that can interact with kernel throughput at these seq sizes.

sam: interesting — rope_theta affecting kernel choice explains why models with identical dimension but different rope defaults are diverging. maybe the selector overweights rope_theta for the head_dim path.

mira: agreed. quick mitigation: add a model-specific override for llama3-13b to prefer legacy head kernel until we patch selector. config snippet: 
```
models:
  llama3-13b:
    runtime_overrides:
      kernel_selector: legacy_head_path
```

alex: that fixed the regression in staging when applied — p95 back to ~100ms. should we roll this as a short-term patch?

sam: yes, roll override and open a bug to refine selector scoring. action items: (1) revert rope_theta weight bump in selector, (2) add head_dim + sequence length cost model, (3) add unit perf test for seq=1024 bs=4 for llama3-13b.

kai: also worth tuning batching: for seq >= 1024 we should lower `max_tokens_per_batch` or increase split_threshold to avoid packing that triggers the frac kernel. proposed runtime patch: 
```
runtime:
  batch:
    max_tokens_per_batch: 8192
    microbatching: true
    split_threshold_tokens: 2048
```

mira: note — RMSNorm and SiLU aren't the root cause here but profiling shows rmsnorm_fwd at 8.7% so small wins possible by kernel fusion later.

alex: filing the bug and adding the override now. i'll post the PR and link here. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: created issue #5421: "kernel_selector: rope_theta overweighting -> llama3-13b p95 regression" (assigned to sam).

sam: i'll take it. plan: add selector unit tests, run against mixtral/mistral variants, and validate on dedicated infra. will also check qwen configs for similar rope defaults.

alex: great — keeping this thread for rollout notes. follow-ups: drop a short blurb in release notes and add a dashboard alert for selector-induced regressions.

mira: ack.

kai: ack.
